head: 77df6cc61596d10c093212933ace4411abcd4610
methodology: Complete file coverage is a static audit: AST-assisted inventories of test operations/assertions/exception expectations and fixture/parameter distinctions, file-specific risk assessments, and targeted deeper source/helper review. It is not a claim of a literal line-by-line manual read of every source byte.

No pytest suite, browser journey, live provider call, external database connection or coverage/mutation run was performed. A direct installer import-checker counterexample was evaluated without starting a watcher or service.
Every test is retained except explicit recommendations; no recommendation has been applied. No production functionality or coding guidelines were changed by this audit.
Counts are Python test functions, before parameter expansion, not collected/executed pytest cases. Test-named support modules with no test functions remain in the file ledger.

The worktree already contained substantial concurrent edits. Three reviewed AL modules moved after the initial inventory; their current reviewed hashes are retained. Recommendations apply to the recorded file hashes.
proposed_testing_standards: State the behavior and regression risk each test protects; inspect the production path before changing or deleting it.
Assert observable outputs, state changes and failure outcomes. A symbol, file, key or phrase alone is insufficient unless the existence/shape is itself a meaningful shipped contract.
Preserve security, business rules, edge cases and fixed regressions. Retain uncertain tests and record the concern.
Delete duplicates only after comparing fixtures, parameters, environment/platform guards, helper assertions and all unique checks. Transfer unique assertions before consolidation.
Make invariant loops non-vacuous: require the expected result or scenario before applying all/for assertions.
Use before/after evidence for change claims; compare to a value observed before the mutation, and measure writes on the actual connection or persisted state.
Make tests independent of ordering and unrelated test side effects. Put always-needed diagnostics in fixtures rather than passing metadata-only tests.
Static prompt, schema, packaging, parity and closed-inventory checks can be valuable product contracts; retain those intentionally, while testing runtime consequences where feasible.
Distinguish synthetic/fixture, integration and actual browser/provider evidence. Do not count a disabled parser, source substring or zero exit as proof of unexercised behavior.
During browser execution also inspect layout, overflow, focus, scroll, accessibility and interaction; retain one meaningful full user journey when extracting focused checks.
